paragraphs.text: Good afternoon, sisters and elders. I was able to enjoy his own interviews again today with about 20 of you. I really love having these interviews. It's not quite as good as seeing you in person, but it's still wonderful. You bring a smile to my face every time I start that video call. Thank you for showing your true values in this day of confinement. It would be easy to just be wasting your time, but I know you are not doing that. You are showing what you're really made of, and it's great.

There's no real new updates today, but I did want to remind you that if your landlord is asking you about the rent check or somehow giving you a little hint that he or she would kind of like to get paid, please go ahead and go right up to them and tell them that we've got those checks, they're sitting right on my desk right now, I'm looking at them right now. I love to get those checks to them. I just don't know how to get the ones up in the Bulacan and San Jose del Monte areas. I just don't know how to get them there.

If your landlord has a way of getting down here, all they've got to do is let you know, you let me know, and I'll meet them anywhere and get them that check. If we can't figure it out as soon as this quarantine is over, I'll rush those checks to them so that they don't have to worry, but we certainly want to have them be able to rest easy that we're going to pay the bills because we have integrity and we want them to know that.
Speaking of integrity, I want to share a story with you. I heard many, many years ago that really had an impact on me and I hope it's a blessing to you.

Once upon a time, an aging king woke up one day very aware of his own mortality. He was getting old and he knew that one day soon he would die. He had no son and his was the culture where only a male heir could take his place. He decided that he would adopt a son who would then become the new king, but he insisted that such an adopted son must be extraordinary in every sense of the word. He considered each of his advisors and relatives in turn, but found none of them really stacked up to be the kind of person that he wanted to leave the kingdom to.

So he launched a competition in his kingdom. It was open to all the boys, no matter what their background, whether they were boys from the rich people or the poor people, the city people or the country people, it didn't matter. Everybody could compete.
Ten boys made it to the very top and the very final and there was very little to separate these boys in terms of their intelligence or physical attributes or capabilities. They were all amazing.

The king said to them, "I have just one last test and whoever comes top in this last test will become my adopted son and heir to my throne." Then he said, "this kingdom depends solely on agriculture. So the king must know how to cultivate plants. Here are seven seeds of grain for each of you. Take them home, plant them and nurture them for the next six weeks. At the end of six weeks, we shall see who has done the best job of cultivating the grain. That person will be my son and my heir and the next king of the kingdom."

Well, the boys took their seeds and hurried home. Each got a pot and prepared the soil and sowed his seeds. There was so much excitement in the kingdom as the people waited to see who was destined to be the next king.

In one home, the boy and his parents were almost heartbroken when the days stretched into weeks and the seeds failed to sprout. The boy did not know what had gone wrong. He had selected the soil carefully. He had applied the right quantity and the type of fertilizer had been very, very dutiful and watering at the right time. He'd even prayed over a day and night and yet his seeds had turned out to be unproductive.

Some of his friends advised him to go and buy seeds from the market and plant that. After all, they said, how can anyone tell the seeds of grain from one from another? But his parents, who had always taught him the value of integrity, reminded him that if the king wanted them to plant just any grain, he would have asked them to go for their own seed. They said, "if you take anything different from what the king gave you, that would be dishonest. Maybe we're not destined for you to be on the throne and to be king. If so, let it be. But don't be found to have deceived the king," they said to him.

Well, the appointed day came and the boys returned to the palace, each of them proudly exhibiting a pot of healthy seedlings. It was obvious that the other nine boys had had great success with their seeds.

The king began making his way down the line of eager boys and asked each of them, "is this what came out of the seeds I gave you?" And each boy responded, "yes, your majesty." And the king would nod and move down the line.

The king finally got to the last boy in the lineup. The boy was shaking. He was so afraid. He feared that the king might have him thrown into prison for wasting his seeds. The king said, "what did you do with the seeds I gave you?"
"I planted them. I cared for them diligently, your majesty, but alas, they failed to sprout." The boy hung his head in shame and the crowd jeered and mocked him.
But the king raised his hands and signaled for silence. Then he said, "my people, behold, your next king."

The people were confused. Why that one? I mean, how could he be the right choice? The king took his place up on the throne with the boy by his side and said, "I gave these boys boiled seeds. This test was not for cultivating grain. It was a test of character, a test of integrity. It was the ultimate test. If a king must have one quality, it must be that he should be above dishonesty. Only this boy passed the test."

So dear elders and sisters, I share this story with you as a compliment to you. You are showing the Lord that you have integrity. Every day that you choose to find a way to do good, to lift up another person, to strengthen their hope and their faith, to keep going, to keep getting better, to keep using your time wisely, you're putting yourself in a position so that the real king will say to you someday, "well done, thou good and faithful servant, enter into my rest."
Good night, elders and sisters. I love you all for who you are and who you are becoming.
